 (Goldi s/o Rajendraprasad Gupta Vs. State of Maharashtra and anr.)

__________________________________________________________________________

and Registrar's Orders.
Shri S.A. Mohta, Advocate for applicant.

Shri T.A. Mirza, App for non-applicant Nos.1 & 2.
 Coram : V. M. Deshpande And
 Anil S. Kilor, Jj.
Date : 5th October, 2020.
Hearing was conducted through Video conferencing and the learned counsel agreed that the audio and visual quality was proper.

2. Heard Shri T.A. Mirza, the learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the applicants Nos.1 &
2/State and Food Safety Officer, in this application and Shri S.A. Mohta, the learned counsel for non-applicant/ accused.
3.

Shri Mirza, learned Additional Public Prosecutor points out that this application has been moved on behalf of the State and the Food Safety Officer, making a prayer to vacate the interim order dated 03.09.2019 or in alternative clarify the interim 9.apl887.2019.odt order dated 03.09.2019 and allow the original non- applicant No.2/Food Safety Officer to file the prosecution under Section 42 of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006, against the applicant/accused.
4. Shri Mirza, learned Additional Public Prosecutor has drawn attention of this Court to the orders Goldi S/O Rajendraprasad Gupta vs State Of Mah., Thr. Pso Ps Kelwad Tq ...

sentences.text:
on 5 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164704337/
1 passed by this Court in identical matters, allowing the Food Safety Officer to file prosecution under Section 42 of the Act, 2006.
5.

Shri Mohta, learned counsel for the non- applicant in this application, is not disputing the fact that in identical matters, this Court permitted the Food Safety Officer to file prosecution under Section 42 of the Act, 2006.

However, he points out that in the present matter, the crime has been registered for the offences punishable under Section 272, 273, 328 of the Indian Penal Code alongwith the offences under Section 26(i), 26(2)(iv), 27(3)(e) and 30(2)(A) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
6. We have perused the record and the orders passed by this Court in similar matters.

It is clear from the record that this Court in identical matters, has permitted the Food Safety Officer to prosecute the persons like the non-applicant in the present application 9.apl887.2019.odt under Section 42 of the Act, 2006.
7.

In that view of the matter and in view of the fact that the non-applicant in this application can challenge the chargesheet, we are of the opinion that the interim order granted by this Court on 03.09.2019 shall be modified in the following terms:
(i) The Criminal Application (APPP) No.962/2020 is allowed.
(ii) The Investigating Agency shall file chargesheet, as assured, within 1  month from today.
The Food Safety Officer, will be at liberty to file complaint under the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
(iii) We have not delved into the issue raised by the original applicant.
It will be open for the original applicant/non-applicant in this application to avail appropriate remedy for redressal of his grievances, as per law after filing of the chargesheet.
8. The criminal application is disposed of in above terms.
JUDGE JUDGE Prity Goldi S/O
Rajendraprasad Gupta vs State Of Mah., Thr. Pso Ps Kelwad Tq
